Recent diffusion RL methods optimize image-level rewards, yet diffusion models generate images through hundreds of intermediate denoising predictions. This creates a fundamental supervision gap:

How can endpoint rewards effectively guide intermediate denoising steps?

In 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗢𝗣𝗦𝗗, we introduce On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), a new diffusion post-training paradigm that converts image-level reward guidance into explicit intermediate supervision. Reward-guided targets are constructed at sampled denoising queries and continuously refreshed as the policy evolves.

More importantly, we show that target construction and finite optimization are fundamentally different problems—a target with higher reward improvement does not necessarily produce a better optimization update. This suggests a new evaluation principle for diffusion RL.

Across SD3.5-M and Z-Image-Turbo, 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗢𝗣𝗦𝗗 achieves the best held-out performance in 19/20 reward-matched settings, improves over the strongest baseline by up to 44%, and reduces training GPU-hours by 40–63% compared with DiffusionNFT.

We hope this work provides a new perspective on making diffusion post-training both more effective and more interpretable.

Feedback and discussions are very welcome!

"On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models"

Diffusion RL gets a reward only after the final image, even though the model actually acts through many intermediate denoising steps.

DiffusionOPSD turns that endpoint reward into explicit reward-improving targets at the model’s own intermediate states, then distills those targets back into the model and continually refreshes them on-policy.

Across two diffusion backbones and ten evaluators, it gets the best held-out score in 19 of 20 settings while cutting training GPU-hours by up to 63%.

The key idea is treating diffusion alignment less like noisy trajectory-level RL and more like continuously refreshed self-distillation with direct intermediate supervision.
